regime.title: US evidence rules — authentication of electronic evidence (FRE 901, 902, proposed 707; 28 U.S.C. § 1746)

source.citation: Federal Rules of Evidence 901(b)(9), 902(11), 902(13), 902(14) and proposed 707; 28 U.S.C. § 1746
source.note: law.cornell.edu and govinfo.gov were unreachable when this map was written; rule numbers follow common citation and are unverified; requirement text is our paraphrase

preamble: FRE 707 is a proposal; its current status is unverified.

rows.requirement: Evidence about a process or system can show that it produces an accurate result.
A record offered on a written declaration needs reasonable written notice to the other side, with the record and declaration made available.
rows.mechanism: The kit carries the record and a draft declaration.
rows.operator_action: Serve written notice and make the record available.

rows.requirement: A record generated by an electronic process, or copied from a device by a process of digital identification, can be self-authenticating on the certification of a qualified person.
rows.mechanism: Draft certifications and the hash recipe.
rows.limits: Drafts for a person to review and sign; no legal advice.

rows.requirement: An unsworn declaration made under penalty of perjury can stand in for a sworn one.
rows.mechanism: The kit carries a draft for the person who verified.
rows.operator_action: The person who verified completes and signs the declaration.

rows.requirement: A proposed rule would hold machine-generated analytic output to the reliability standard for expert testimony.
rows.mechanism: Per-ruleset validation sheets packaged with the claims in a kit.
